answer: A wharf in hollow holds no identity until it renews, and each renewal burns atlas equal to the live wharf count in hollow, read atomically at renewal, so a thousand clones set the rate to a thousand and each burns a thousand atlas per epoch just to keep standing. Splitting income buys nothing because the rate is global, not per-clone, and no batch settles two renewals on one read. The bill is atlas burned by every wharf, every epoch, indexed to headcount; a lapsed renewal forfeits the seat. It breaks if renewals settle off-registry or dormant wharfs keep standing.
